name: GRIT DOUBLE
author: Niklas Wallin
shortDesc: Tight doubler with grit — thickens a single-coil lead
desc: A close doubler that adds body and edge to a lead vocal over electric guitar. Dialled in with a single-coil guitar (Strat or Tele) direct into the device, medium input gain. The subtle pitch variation gives it a tape-doubled character rather than a clinical copy. Works well for rock, blues and rootsy styles where a big, live vocal sound matters more than pristine accuracy. Bring the Mix knob down slightly if the doubling effect is too obvious in your room.

name: METAL FIFTH
author: Anders Bjork
shortDesc: Aggressive fifth harmony — designed for dropped tunings
desc: A fifth-interval harmony optimised for heavy rock and metal. The harmony voice has a slightly brighter character to stay intelligible over high-gain guitar. Tested on a humbucker guitar in drop-D tuning running through a high-gain amp sim. The Humanize is turned down to near-zero so the harmony tracks fast, aggressive phrasing cleanly. Do not expect this to sound natural — it is meant to be heard, not hidden.

name: INDIE ROOM
author: Chloe Farrand
shortDesc: Washy room reverb with chorus — hazy indie sound
desc: A lush combination of room reverb and subtle chorus on the voice. The result is that slightly out-of-focus vocal sound common in indie and shoegaze recordings. Dialled in for a dynamic microphone at moderate distance to add some air. Works very well over jangly clean guitar parts. The chorus depth is intentionally low — this is about creating a sense of space rather than an obvious modulation effect.

name: BLUES DOUBLE
author: Ray Fontaine
shortDesc: Warm doubler for blues and soul — subtle but present
desc: A smooth doubler with slightly more spread than a tight slap-double. Designed for blues and soul performances where you want the vocal to feel bigger without obviously hearing the effect. Built around an SM7B microphone at close range. The pitch variance is slightly higher than a precision doubler — it adds a human quality that suits soulful, expressive singing well. Keep the Mix at around 30-40% for best results.
